transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Avery Kim (Redwood CSM); Maya Patel (Oakridge CISO), Evan Brooks (CTO), Ravi Menon (Security Eng), Lena Ortiz (Legal)

Summary:
Short security & privacy review focusing on SOC2/ISO posture, RBAC and SSO, audit log retention & access, encryption/KMS, data residency, and explicit confirmation about prompt/content retention and training-on-customer-data. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share SOC2 artifact, KMS docs, sample audit logs; Oakridge to share PHI classification and contract redlines; schedule follow-up legal call.

Topics:
- SOC 2 Type II and ISO readiness
- RBAC, SSO (SAML/Okta), SCIM provisioning
- Audit logs (token-level, per-route) and log retention policies
- Encryption at rest and in transit, KMS/HSM integrations
- Data residency and VPC/private deployment options
- Prompt/content retention policy, PII/PHI safeguards, and "no training on customer data" guarantee

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Lee from Redwood, AE. We'll walk through our security posture and answer questions. Priya's with me for the technical details.
[00:15] Maya: Thanks Jordan, I'm Maya, CISO at Oakridge. We have Lena from legal and Ravi our security engineer. We mostly want to confirm how you handle PHI and that data isn't used to train models, plus technical details on KMS and audit logs.
[00:30] Jordan: Totally, that's the goal. Priya, do you want to take the KMS and retention bit?
[00:34] Priya: Sure. Quick note, apologies in advance if my mic is a bit echo-y. So on encryption: Redwood encrypts all customer data in transit using TLS 1.2+ and at rest using AES-256. For keys we integrate with customer-managed KMS---AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM options for Private deployments. We also support Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) for Dedicated and Private.
[01:05] Ravi: When you say integrate, does Redwood ever hold plaintext keys or escrow keys? We need to understand key lifecycle and whether Redwood can decrypt without our consent.
[01:15] Priya: Good question. For hosted deployments we can be configured with a customer KMS where Redwood stores only encrypted blobs and never persist plaintext keys. For Private/VPC installs the keys stay in the customer's KMS; Redwood requests short-lived Data Encryption Keys via KMS APIs. We do not store customer key material in plaintext. In Dedicated we can do isolated key access policies; again, no persistent plaintext keys on our side.
[01:35] Evan: Is there an HSM-backed option?
[01:38] Priya: Yes, HSM options are available for Private installs. We can show the HSM integration diagram in the follow-up.
[01:44] Lena: For SOC2 artifacts, are you willing to share the Type II report and any ISO attestation?
[01:50] Jordan: Yes, we'll share the SOC 2 Type II report and our ISO documentation checklist. I'll attach those to the follow-up email --- link to the secure binder.
[02:00] Maya: Great. Next --- audit logs. We need per-route and per-token level tracing for compliance. What granularity do you provide and retention options?
[02:12] Priya: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns and we surface request/response metadata in the audit logs---timestamps, request IDs, model used, route, and user identity. For security/audit logs we log metadata and events, not raw customer prompts by default for long-term retention. Short-term logs used for debugging can include snippet redactions. Retention windows are configurable --- e.g., 30/90/365 days --- and for certain enterprise tiers we offer longer retention behind an add-on.
[02:47] Ravi: Clarify "not raw prompts by default" --- are transcripts stored? If so, where and for how long? Our policy is strict about PHI.
[02:56] Priya: Under our default hosted model, full request content is retained for X days for operational debugging and abuse monitoring --- we can set that to a low window for Oakridge or use Private deployment where content never leaves the VPC. Important: Redwood has a documented "no training on customer data" policy --- we do not use customer prompts or outputs to retrain public models. We can provide contractual language and SOC attestation for that.
[03:30] Maya: Can you confirm that as a contractual clause --- that none of our content will be used to train models, and particularly PHI won't be used in any training?
[03:36] Jordan: Yes. We provide a no-training clause option in enterprise contracts. For Private and Dedicated, it's default that we don't train on customer data. For hosted, we can agree to strict non-training commitments and data isolation in the contract. We'll have legal language for Lena.
[03:52] Lena: We'll need explicit wording and artifact. Also: deletion guarantees and data handling in backups.
[03:58] Priya: We can include data deletion SLAs for the pilot --- e.g., on deletion request, removable within N days, and for backups we can provide certification of removal from live backups as part of the process. We'll provide the exact mechanics in the follow-up.
[04:15] Evan: On-prem or VPC deployment --- what's the difference in terms of telemetry and logs? If we go VPC, do you still get telemetry?
[04:25] Priya: For Private/VPC, the control plane is customer-managed and telemetry can be forwarded to the customer's logging stack. Redwood will have a minimal control plane footprint for orchestration, but we can restrict telemetry collection. For Dedicated, logs are accessible to both parties under agreed policies; we can restrict sensitive fields.
[04:44] Ravi: How about RBAC and SSO? We require SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning.
[04:50] Jordan: We support SSO via SAML and OIDC and SCIM for user provisioning. Role-based access controls are supported in the Console---per-route and per-team roles, admin/editor/viewer. We can map SCIM groups to RBAC roles.
[05:05] Ravi: Are roles audited? We need change history for approvals.
[05:09] Priya: Yes, role changes are captured in the audit log with before/after snapshots and user identity. We can provide exportable audit logs for your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog).
[05:22] Maya: Data residency --- we need EU data residency for certain PHI-like datasets and US-only for others. How do you support region pinning?
[05:31] Priya: We support region pinning for both hosted and Dedicated --- requests can be routed to region-specific clusters, and for Private we can deploy into your region or on-prem. We'll need to capture the specific datasets and routes for the PoC to ensure proper routing.
[05:48] Evan: What about model variants and fallback --- does that ever route data to another region if capacity is constrained?
[05:56] Priya: We have routing policies that can be configured by tenant. For Oakridge we'll set a strict policy: no cross-region fallback for region-locked models. If capacity is constrained we'll fail-open to a degraded mode or return a capacity error rather than route out-of-region.
[06:12] Ravi: Logging detail: do you log full response bodies in audit logs?
[06:16] Priya: Default enterprise logs capture metadata and a truncated response preview. Full response bodies are considered sensitive; we only retain them if explicitly enabled and with strict access controls. For PHI workloads we recommend Private deployment or disabling full-response retention.
[06:32] Maya: On the "no training" point, can you explain how you enforce that internally? Is there a flag that prevents any data from entering training pipelines?
[06:39] Priya: Yes --- we have explicit data handling flags per tenant and dedicated ingestion pipelines. Customer data marked as protected is isolated and excluded from any training buckets. Access controls and monitoring prevent export of that data. We also include it in our SOC 2 scope and change control process.
[06:55] Jordan: Just to add: we rotate keys, enforce least privilege, and perform internal reviews. We'll provide the change management attestation.
[07:05] Lena: For contracts, we'll need indemnities around data breach and PHI. Also, do you support BAA (Business Associate Agreement)?
[07:13] Jordan: We can sign a BAA; Redwood has precedent BAAs for healthcare customers. We'll share a template with standard HIPAA/BAA terms for Oakridge to review.
[07:22] Ravi: If we run a PoC, can we collect sample audit logs and see the Console dashboards? We want to validate the RBAC and log exports.
[07:29] Priya: Absolutely. For the PoC we can provision a sandbox tenant in Dedicated or Private; we'll generate sample audit logs and a read-only view for your team to confirm.
[07:38] Maya: One last question on retention windows --- you mentioned configurable retention; do you have an SLA on log availability?
[07:46] Priya: We guarantee ingestion within our SLA for Dedicated, and retention is configurable. For longer retention we use cold storage with retrieval SLAs; specifics will be in the follow-up doc.
[07:55] Eva (sic) [possible transcript error]: Can you confirm how deletions propagate to backups?
[07:59] Priya: We'll include the backup deletion flow in the security binder --- typically deletion requests mark data for removal and we rotate keys for orphaned backups, then schedule physical removal per policy. We'll provide the exact timeline in writing.
[08:15] Jordan: Ok, quick recap of action items and next steps: I'll send SOC2 and ISO binder; Priya will share KMS/HSM diagrams and sample audit logs; Oakridge will share PHI classification and legal will send contract redlines. We'll aim to reconvene after legal has reviewed.
[08:33] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:36] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

End of transcript.
